results.title: Ergonomics and the Aging Workforce: Strategies for Creating Safe and Productive Workplaces – International Journal of Research and Innovation in Social Science
results.content: # Ergonomics and the Aging Workforce: Strategies for Creating Safe and Productive Workplaces. As the global workforce ages, addressing the ergonomic needs of older workers has become an essential aspect of promoting safety, health, and productivity in the workplace. Findings suggest that workplace adjustments, such as adjustable furniture, improved lighting, and more frequent breaks, are effective in mitigating the physical challenges faced by older workers. This research aims to explore the connection between ergonomic design and the aging workforce, identifying key factors that can influence the safety, well-being, and productivity of older workers. The objective is to provide organizations with actionable insights on how to tailor their work environments to accommodate the specific needs of an aging workforce while ensuring productivity and reducing the risk of injury. The growing body of literature on ergonomics and the aging workforce underscores the importance of workplace design in mitigating the physical and cognitive challenges associated with aging.

results.title: Effectiveness of workplace interventions for health promotion - ScienceDirect
results.content: # Review Effectiveness of workplace interventions for health promotion. Author links open overlay panel, , , ,. https://doi.org/10.1016/S2468-2667(25)00095-700095-7 "Persistent link using digital object identifier")Get rights and content. Although the effectiveness of workplace health promotion has been evaluated in reviews focusing on specific interventions, a comprehensive overview is needed. To address this gap, we present a quality-informed horizontal analysis encompassing 88 reviews and 339 meta-analysed effect estimates published between 2011 and 2024, covering a broad range of workplace health interventions. Mindfulness showed effectiveness across multiple stress and mental health outcomes, and cognitive behavioural techniques, stress management, physically oriented methods, and e-health interventions also showed some effectiveness. A variety of behavioural, physical activity, environmental, multicomponent, and e-health interventions influenced physical activity and sedentary time at work. In this Review we also discuss the broader public health implications of workplace health promotion, and highlight the strengths and limitations of the existing evidence and propose directions for future research.
